label: Essential-state event and prior…: An event is a change from one state of affairs to another with…
term: essential-state event and prior explanatory cause (survey A3)
definition: An event is a change from one state of affairs to another with those states essential to its identity. A3P1 describes a cause as a prior condition capable of explaining or partly explaining an event; A3C describes a prior condition that explains or partly explains something else. Possible causability of the SAME event must preserve its essential states. Neither wording alone defines a concrete individual bearer, temporal presence or complete explanatory sufficiency.
note: Declaration-completion investigation (2026-11-09): original A3_EVENT_IDENTITY_CAUSAL_PRIORITY_1 remains unmapped. Essential before/after states give a necessary constraint on event identity, not the converse that matching state contents suffice for identical events. Owner choice pending: identify events with ordered structured state contents, or permit distinct occurrences with the same contents and specify the additional cross-history identity criterion. TruthCore.Causality.EventStatePreservation keeps occurrences separate from Content and proves only preservation and scope controls; it is not the original sense declaration. Prior condition remains a supplied relation: no temporal concrete bearer, actuality, complete sufficiency or actual universal causation follows. Scenario.CausalOpportunityAt permits an analogous beginning and is not a same-event dictionary.
